title: Fort Ontario Study Act
official_summary:
Fort Ontario Study Act

(Sec. 3) This bill directs the Department of the Interior to conduct a special resource study of Fort Ontario in Oswego, New York.

Interior shall: (1) evaluate the fort's national significance, and (2) determine the suitability and feasibility of designating it as a unit of the National Park System.

summary.headline: A 2018 law directs the Interior Department to study whether Fort Ontario in Oswego, New York, should become a national park unit.
summary.what_it_does: The law orders the Department of the Interior to run a special resource study of Fort Ontario. The study must judge how nationally significant the fort is. It must also decide whether making the fort a unit of the National Park System is suitable and feasible. The law itself does not add the fort to the park system.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Oswego, New York, and nearby communities
who_it_affects.how: They may be affected by the study's findings if the fort is later considered for park designation, though the summary does not describe any specific local change.
A future park designation could change how the fort is visited and managed, but the study comes first and no designation is made by this law.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect on enactment, October 9, 2018. The summary does not give a deadline for completing the study.
